title: Euler characteristic of an invertible twist on an integral proper curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module] and $\mathcal F$ a coherent $\mathcal O_C$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $\xi$ be the generic point, characterized by $\overline{\{\xi\}}=C$. Its local ring is the residue field $\mathcal O_{C,\xi}=\kappa(\xi)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Set $r=\dim_{\kappa(\xi)}\mathcal F_\xi$, the finite dimension of the generic stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk, def-weil-vector-space-dimension]. For the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], Euler characteristic [def-pc-euler-characteristic] and degree [def-pc-degree-line-bundle],
$$\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathcal O_C}\mathcal F)=r\deg_k(\mathcal L)+\chi(C,\mathcal F).$$
The generic rank $r$ may be zero; no local freeness of $\mathcal F$ or smoothness of $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, specialization to an invertible first factor (n=1).

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its spectrum is a one-point affine scheme [def-weil-affine-spectrum], hence quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Properness gives that $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $C$ Noetherian. The module $\mathcal O_C$ is quasi-coherent of finite type, hence coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Fix $\mathcal L$. On every open trivializing $\mathcal L$, the tensor $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal H$ by $a\otimes h\mapsto ah$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Thus it is coherent whenever $\mathcal H$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. A finite local generating set for $\mathcal H$ gives a finite generating set of $\mathcal H_\xi$ by taking germs [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; since $\mathcal O_{C,\xi}=\kappa(\xi)$ is a field, its dimension $r(\mathcal H)$ is finite. Set $D(\mathcal H)=\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H)-\chi(C,\mathcal H)-r(\mathcal H)\deg_k\mathcal L$, and let $\mathcal P(\mathcal H)$ mean $D(\mathcal H)=0$. For the zero module its tensor, stalk and cohomology groups are zero, so $\mathcal P(0)$ holds [def-pc-euler-characteristic].

source.place: Tag 0AYV, lemma-degree-on-proper-curve, proof: define the property P; Noetherian and coherence hypotheses made explicit using 01T6 and 01XZ.

proof.text: Consider a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal H_1\to\mathcal H_2\to\mathcal H_3\to0$ of coherent modules. The invertible module $\mathcal L$ is finite locally free of rank one [def-sc-invertible-module]. By [lem-sc-ext-tensor-exact], tensoring this sequence on the left with $\mathcal L$ gives a short exact sequence. Its terms are coherent by Step 1. Apply the first assertion of [lem-pc-euler-additive] to both sequences to obtain $\chi(C,\mathcal H_2)=\chi(C,\mathcal H_1)+\chi(C,\mathcal H_3)$ and $\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_2)=\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_1)+\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal H_3)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, proof of condition (1); Tag 08AA, lemma-euler-characteristic-additive.

proof.text: Taking stalks at $\xi$ in the sequence of Step 2 gives a short exact sequence of finite-dimensional $\kappa(\xi)$-vector spaces by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact], including the injectivity and surjectivity assertions. A basis of $(\mathcal H_1)_\xi$, mapped into $(\mathcal H_2)_\xi$, together with arbitrary lifts of a basis of $(\mathcal H_3)_\xi$, is a basis of $(\mathcal H_2)_\xi$: subtract the lifted image to prove spanning, and apply the quotient map to prove independence. Counting these basis elements [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] gives $r(\mathcal H_2)=r(\mathcal H_1)+r(\mathcal H_3)$. Substitution in Step 2 yields $D(\mathcal H_2)=D(\mathcal H_1)+D(\mathcal H_3)$. Consequently if any two of these three integers vanish then the third vanishes. This verifies the two-out-of-three condition for $\mathcal P$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, proof of condition (1): additivity of generic rank; Modules 01AG for exact stalks.

proof.text: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow C$ be an integral closed subscheme, and $z$ its generic point. Its underlying set is an irreducible closed subset [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. If $z\ne\xi$, this subset is proper. It cannot contain a point $y\ne z$: because $z$ is generic, $\overline{\{y\}}\subsetneq Z\subsetneq C$ would be a chain of irreducible closed subsets of length two, contradicting $\dim C=1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus $Z$ is the closed singleton $\{z\}$. If $z=\xi$, the image of $Z$ is all of $C$. On an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the integral scheme $C$, the closed subscheme is $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and its image contains the generic prime $(0)$, so $I\subseteq(0)$ and $I=0$. These local descriptions identify $i$ with the identity of $C$. In the singleton case, take an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $z$. The integral quotient $A/I$ has only one prime ideal, so that ideal is $(0)$ and is maximal; hence $A/I$ is a field. The corresponding ideal of $A$ is the maximal ideal of $z$, so $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$, with its reduced closed-point structure [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tag 0AYV, proof of condition (2): Z is X or a closed point; affine quotient and dimension-chain details.

proof.text: For $Z=C$, choose $\mathcal G=\mathcal O_C$. It is coherent by Step 1, its support is $C$ because every local ring is nonzero, and its generic stalk is the one-dimensional field $\kappa(\xi)$. The maximal ideal of that field is zero, so it annihilates the generic stalk [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Finally $\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal O_C\cong\mathcal L$ by $l\otimes a\mapsto al$, with inverse $l\mapsto l\otimes1$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $\deg_k\mathcal L=\chi(C,\mathcal L)-\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Thus $D(\mathcal O_C)=0$. This supplies all four required properties of the witness for $Z=C$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, proof of condition (2), case Z=X; Tag 0AYR, definition-degree-invertible-sheaf.

proof.text: For $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$ at a closed point $z\ne\xi$, choose $\mathcal G=i_*\mathcal O_Z$. Both $C$ and the one-point field scheme $Z$ are locally Noetherian, and $\mathcal O_Z$ is coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] therefore makes $\mathcal G$ coherent and identifies its support with $\{z\}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks], its stalk at $z$ is $\kappa(z)$, with $\mathcal O_{C,z}$-action through the residue map [def-weil-residue-field]; this stalk is killed by $\mathfrak m_z$ and has dimension one over $\kappa(z)$. The same stalk lemma gives $\mathcal G_\xi=0$, because $\xi\notin\{z\}$, so $r(\mathcal G)=0$. All the support and generic-stalk requirements of the closed-point witness are now verified.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, proof of condition (2), closed-point witness i_*O_Z; coherent 087T and sheaves 00AE.

proof.text: The support $\{z\}$ in Step 6 has dimension zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Apply the last clause of [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] on the proper scheme $C$ to the coherent module $\mathcal G$ and the invertible module $\mathcal L$. It gives $\chi(C,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L)=\chi(C,\mathcal G)$. The balanced maps $g\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes g$ and $l\otimes g\mapsto g\otimes l$ give inverse sheaf isomorphisms [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Cohomology sends inverse maps to inverse maps, so their Euler characteristics agree [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Thus $\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal G)=\chi(C,\mathcal G)$; together with $r(\mathcal G)=0$ this is $D(\mathcal G)=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, proof of condition (2), closed-point calculation; Tag 0AYT, lemma-chi-tensor-finite, clause (5) with n=1.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-coherent-property-devissage] on the Noetherian scheme $C$ to the property $\mathcal P$ of Step 1. Its condition (0) was checked there; its two-out-of-three condition (1) was checked in Steps 2 and 3; and Step 4 lists every integral closed subscheme, for which Steps 5 through 7 supply a coherent witness with the required support, annihilated generic stalk of residue-field dimension one, and property $\mathcal P$. The theorem gives $D(\mathcal F)=0$ for the given coherent module $\mathcal F$. Expanding this equality gives $\chi(C,\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal F)=r\deg_k\mathcal L+\chi(C,\mathcal F)$, including $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYV, final application of Cohomology of Schemes Tag 01YI, lemma-property.

lean.statement: theorem eulerChar_tensor_invertible_generic_rank (k : Type u) [Field k] (C : Scheme.{u}) [C.Over (Spec (.of k))] [IsIntegral C] [IsProper (C ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hdim : topologicalKrullDim C = 1) (L : C.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (F : C.Modules) (hF : RingedSpace.IsCoherent C.toRingedSpace F) (ξ : C) (hξ : closure ({ξ} : Set C) = Set.univ) : (L ⊗ F).eulerChar k = (Module.finrank (C.presheaf.stalk ξ) (F.presheaf.stalk ξ) : ℤ) * L.degree k + F.eulerChar k
